title: A printf subset
description:
Implement part of `printf` by reading its man page carefully.

```
fmt("%d|%5d|%-5d|%05d", 42, 42, 42, 42) -> 42|   42|42   |00042
fmt("%s and %c", "tea", '!')           -> tea and !
fmt("%x %X %%", 255, 255)              -> ff FF %
fmt("%q", 1)                            -> error: unknown conversion q
```
hints: Parse each conversion as: `%`, flags, width digits, the conversion letter (lesson 4.04).
The man page says `0` is ignored when `-` is also given; that is the kind of detail worth testing.

A `std::variant<long, std::string, char>` (from `<variant>`) holds one of the three types. `std::holds_alternative<long>(arg)` asks which one it holds, and `std::get<long>(arg)` reads it (and throws `std::bad_variant_access` if it holds another type, which is a good "wrong argument type" error).
requirements: Conversions `d`, `s`, `c`, `x`, `X` and `%%`, with the flags `-` and `0` and a width.
Take the arguments as a `std::vector<std::variant<long, std::string, char>>`.
Check each result against the real `std::snprintf`.
